name: Slow Cooker Mississippi Pork Bowls
intro_html: Mississippi pork is that tangy, buttery, ranch-and-pepperoncini magic, and it works just as well on pork as it does on the classic pot roast. Piled over potatoes with carrots, each bowl brings 52 grams of protein for about $3.62 (at everyday cost). Fourteen servings out of one pot keeps the whole week covered.
ingredients_display: Au Jus Gravy Mix: 1 (1 oz) packet (65 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_closing_html: About $3.62 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
shop_smart: Potatoes are one of the cheapest bases going. An 8 lb bag runs cheap and doubles as your starch, so skip buying rice for this one.
One packet of ranch seasoning does all the flavor work. No need for a cabinet full of separate spices.
A jar of pepperoncini lasts a long time in the fridge, so the third of a jar you use here costs next to nothing per bowl.
make_it: Set the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker and surround it with the potatoes and shredded carrots.
Sprinkle the ranch seasoning mix and the au jus gravy mix over everything.
Add the pepperoncini along with a splash of their juice, then lay the butter on top.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork and potatoes are tender.
Shred the pork and stir it through all those buttery, tangy juices.
Whisk the cornstarch with a splash of cold water, stir it into the juices, and let them bubble a minute or two until the sauce thickens.
Divide the pork and potatoes into your containers.
portion_html: Every serving comes in around 550 calories with 52 grams of protein.
credit_html: Recipe adapted from Salt & Lavender, rebuilt for 14-serving budget meal prep with weighed portions and Omaha pricing.
upsell_html: Tangy, hearty, and dead simple. Set it in the morning and dinner takes care of itself. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
